extracted.intended_audience: students and researchers of media studies and journalism (including advanced journalism students and scholars)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and enumerates the many organizational, professional, legal, ideological, routine, and technological factors the book identifies as shaping news/media content — i.e., dimensions one would attend to when evaluating or studying news production and content. Suitable for content-analysis, newsroom studies, and media-critique work.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Amendment freedoms
rubrics_metrics.description: First Amendment freedoms (202-203).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal protection for speech/press that shapes controls/censorship and what journalists can publish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of Information rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Freedom of Information rules, 205.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural/legal mechanism affecting access to government information and thus news reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations and laws in the United States
rubrics_metrics.description: regulations/laws in the United States, 203-205.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory/regulatory constraints on media operations and content (e.g., FCC rules, trafficking rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: International government controls/censorship
rubrics_metrics.description: international, 199-202 (government controls/censorship).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative/legal differences in how governments outside the U.S. regulate and censor media content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trafficking rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Trafficking rule, 204.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific regulatory constraint referenced as shaping broadcast content/advertising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Society of Professional Journalists (SPJ) Code of Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethics, Society of Professional Journalists Code of, 95-97, 100-101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional ethical standards journalists are expected to follow; used as an evaluative touchstone for ethical roles and conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical roles of journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical roles, 95, 98-102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion of different ethical responsibilities (e.g., watchdog, public service) and how they inform practice and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectivity, 4, 112-114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Norm/criterion for journalistic practice (claims of neutrality, balance) and a dimension for evaluating news content and routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: News values
rubrics_metrics.description: News values, 110-112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria (e.g., timeliness, proximity, conflict) that make events newsworthy and influence story selection/placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routines of news production
rubrics_metrics.description: Routines — defined, 105 — including beat/bureaucratic, consumer/audience, event, factory environment of newsrooms, processing of information, routine channels, story structure, sources/suppliers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Types and functions of routines (beat, event, consumer/audience, gatekeeping) that systematically shape what and how news is produced; includes how routines affect selection, processing, and story form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gatekeepers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals or institutional actors who select/screen news; criterion for analyzing who controls flow of information into the public sphere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources and suppliers of news
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources/suppliers — defined, 178; experts, official sources, leaks; selection of sources, 179-182; press releases/conferences, 127-129.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Types of sources (official, expert, leaks, PR materials) and the selection practices that affect content credibility and framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press releases and press conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases/conferences, 127, 128, 129.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How PR-originated materials enter news flow; an evaluative criterion for independence and sourcing practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public relations campaigns and influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Public relations campaigns, 186-189.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organized efforts by actors to shape media coverage; used to assess external influence on news agendas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video news releases (VNRs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Video news releases (VNRs), 99.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepackaged audiovisual material provided to newsrooms — a specific source-type to evaluate for transparency and independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economics and marketplace influences
rubrics_metrics.description: Economics, effects of on content, 143-150; Marketplace influence: competition, marketplace, 209-211; competition and community relations, 212-214.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial incentives, advertising pressures, competition and market structure as determinants of content decisions and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership and corporate structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Ownership — chain versus independent, changes in corporate, cross-ownership, 151, 153, 163-171; ownership issues affecting content and ideology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Who owns media organizations (chains, conglomerates) and ownership changes as a criterion for bias, agenda-setting, and resource allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational role and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization/organizational influence charts, 142-144; role and structure, levels, 140; how large organizations affect content, 156-160; structure effects, 151-156.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal newsroom organization, hierarchy, departments and their impact on content autonomy, priorities, and workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology and platform effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Technology, influence of, 215-219; Internet, 217; electronic highway, 217.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technological affordances and constraints (printing, broadcast, digital) that shape story form, speed, and distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professionalization of journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalism — evolution of, 71-73; as a profession, 92-95; statistics on profession, 63-64.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional norms, training, and occupational identities used as evaluative criteria for competence and role performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and time pressures
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines, effects of, 119.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time constraints influencing verification, depth, and reliance on routine sources; a criterion for assessing reporting quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story structure and news framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Story structure, 114-115; processing of information, content shaped by, 117-127.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative and structural conventions (lead, inverted pyramid, dramatization) that shape meaning and audience interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Values, beliefs and personal orientations of communicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Values and beliefs — effects of communicators' personal, 82-83, 87-91; religious, political, gender, sexual orientation of communicators (66-69, 83-87, 69).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual reporters' and editors' backgrounds and orientations as influences on selection, framing and representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political bias and partisanship
rubrics_metrics.description: Political bias, 42-44; Partisanship, 42-43; political deviance portrayal, 47.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of systematic partisan or ideological slant in coverage; criterion for evaluating fairness and balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideology, hegemony and propaganda models
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideology (defined, 221-222); hegemony, 236-243; propaganda model, 234-236; political economist view, 230-236; power and Marxist paradigm, 228-230.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Macro-level critical perspectives for assessing how media reproduce or challenge dominant power structures and interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest groups and advocacy influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Interest groups, 184-186.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment of organized political/advocacy actors' role in shaping story agendas and source selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and demographic patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Demographic patterns, 52-57; geographic patterns, 49-52; depiction of women, elderly, ethnic groups, sexual orientation, violence, sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative attention to who is represented, how groups are portrayed, and patterns of inclusion/exclusion in coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content categories and symbolic environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Media content categories — surveillance, transmission, entertainment, 28-30; entertainment similarities with news as symbolic environment, 30-31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification of content types as a basis for comparative evaluation (news vs. entertainment, surveillance vs. transmission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement and methodology of content analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Measuring media content, 31-32; Quantitative versus qualitative analysis, 32; methodological bias, 18-19; hypothesis approach, 5-6, 263-270.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological criteria for researching/evaluating media (choice of quantitative vs qualitative, operationalization, bias awareness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manipulation and propaganda techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Manipulation — of reality, visual versus verbal, presidential manipulation; Propaganda, Propaganda Technique in the World War (Lasswell), 34-35.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifying deliberate framing/manipulative techniques and propaganda as evaluative concerns for assessing media integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Groupthink / pack mentality among journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: groupthink/pack mentality of journalists, 122-125, 189-190.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social/process criterion assessing convergence in coverage and reduced critical independence among reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photograph and image manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Photograph manipulation, 100, 251.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual editing/alteration practices as a criterion for assessing authenticity and ethical standards in visual journalism.
